subtitle.zh-TW: 吸菸和癌症一起出現，但吸菸不致癌。
subtitle.en: Smoking and cancer go together, but smoking does not cause cancer.

story.zh-TW: 假設吸菸本身不致癌，但有一種病灶同時讓人想吸菸、也讓人容易得癌症。觀察上，吸菸者得癌症的比例較高；可是若強制改變一個人吸不吸菸，他得癌症的機率不會變。那麼喜歡吸菸的人該不該吸？
story.en: Suppose smoking itself does not cause cancer, but a lesion both makes people want to smoke and makes them prone to cancer. Smokers are observed to get cancer more often; yet forcing a person to smoke or not to smoke would not change their chance of cancer. Should someone who likes to smoke, then, smoke?

zh-TW.sentence: 假設吸菸本身不致癌，但有一種病灶同時讓人想吸菸、也讓人容易得癌症。

en.sentence: Suppose smoking itself does not cause cancer, but a lesion both makes people want to smoke and makes them prone to cancer.

text.zh-TW: 吸不吸菸都改變不了你有沒有病灶；想吸就吸。
text.en: Smoking or not cannot change whether you have the lesion; if you want to smoke, smoke.

explanation.zh-TW: 病灶 L 同時影響人想不想抽菸與有沒有得癌症，抽菸本身不影響癌症。模型用 L 當共同原因，抽菸 S 與癌症 C 各自由 L 加上獨立的外生雜訊決定。這樣在 L 未知時 S 與 C 有相關，但對 S 做介入不改變 C，可用來區分證據決策論與因果決策論。
explanation.en: The lesion L affects both whether a person wants to smoke and whether they get cancer; smoking itself does not affect cancer. The model takes L as the common cause, with smoking S and cancer C each set by L plus independent exogenous noise. So while L is unknown, S and C are correlated, yet intervening on S does not change C. This separates evidential from causal decision theory.

sources.citation: Eells, E. (1982). Rational Decision and Causality. Cambridge University Press.
Egan, A. (2007). Some counterexamples to causal decision theory. Philosophical Review, 116(1), 93–114.
Pearl, J. (2009). Causality: Models, Reasoning, and Inference (2nd ed.). Cambridge University Press.
Skyrms, B. (1980). Causal Necessity. Yale University Press.

label.en: Urge to smoke given no lesion

equations.S: if L then N_S1 else N_S0
equations.C: if L then N_C1 else N_C0

verdicts.note: Equals P(C=1): smoking has no effect.
